utterances.text: And is it true that Milan Lukic didn't insult you or mistreat you while he was questioning for the weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, he did not mistreat me at all. He did raise his voice, but he did not mistreat me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it possible that your husband was alive at this time and maybe in detention somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I asked Milan that night. When he asked me about the weapons, I said, "Where is my husband? Can I see him?" And he said, "You'll know soon enough." He refused to allow me to see him, and he refused to say anything at all: He's alive, he's dead, whatever. I don't know where he was. I don't know if he was alive or not. I would have so dearly loved to know, but I couldn't unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But isn't it true that you testified earlier that -- you said that Milan Lukic said he would check on it, that he would look into it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't remember what you're suggesting. I don't remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, according to your 1994 statement, after this incident you went back to your mother-in-law's place, correct, where she was waiting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And according to your statement, you moved at that point, because you were so frightened, to Baksa's house, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Baksa's, yes. Baksa's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it was after five or six days, although you testified today ten days, that they needed to go to the supermarket for food, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes. Fifteen years is a long time. You can't expect all of the accounts to tally in every little detail. I can't say whether it was five days, ten days. It was roughly five to ten days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But no more than that, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it was during this trip to the supermarket that your mother-in-law was told that all girls had to go to the Hasan Veletovac school in Visegrad, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: The entire family, not just the girls. All of us, their relatives, where they lived with us, for them to take all of us to the Hasan Veletovac school. Hasan Veletovac, that's what the school used to be called back then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you remember where Baksa's house was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Baksa's house was further down the road from the command building. The command was further down, and Baksa's house was further up the road from Dusce, up the hill and then on the way down, well, the house was right there, the third or the fourth house down the road. I can't say exactly, but it was a large house, three floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Had you been there before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, I'd never gone up to the house. I did go to Dusce, to her house, but that was the son's house, meaning Safet's house, her son, the house belonged to him, and she used to stay there, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like you to -- if you were giving me directions to Baksa's house from the police station, could you do that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: The police station now, where it is now? Where it used to be while I was still in Visegrad? Which one do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Oh, of course where it was -- used to be.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: All right. The police station, then past the mosque, which is no longer there, right in the centre of town, and then you would start to walk up the road, up Bikavac, and then you reach the hotel further up, and then you turn right and then straight; you just go on straight, and just off the road, well, there is a large house right there, two adjacent houses, and a third one, Safet's cousin's house, a group of three houses. So that's what path we used to take to reach her place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Which hotel was that, ma'am? What was the name of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is the third house that is Baksa's house less than a hundred metres from this hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think it's a little more. You need to walk some way from there. I can't say how long for, but the path takes you up and then down onto Dusce, so these are some of the last houses before you start going down towards Dusce. So it's towards the very end, one of the last houses, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And after your mother-in-law's return indicating that they wanted all the women to go to the elementary school, you decided to leave, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, not the elementary school. We just wanted to run and hide somewhere because they would be coming to get us. They had described everything, including the houses in which we were staying, so we were meant to go in the opposite direction, run further up, move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And according to your statement, you moved to a house one kilometre away. Can you give us -- or can you tell us how you got to that house and describe sort of in directions how to get to that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: There was the street crossing the whole village, but we didn't take that street, that narrow road. We went between the houses, looking for a house that was empty. So near the top of Bikavac itself, we found a house and we stopped there, my entire family and Baksa Ramovic's family. We went straight up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And then that's when the woman from Zupa arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And then according to your statement, you say that you -- "We stayed the night, and no one disturbed us. The following evening was the 27th of June, 1992." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What happened to the 20 days that are in between that? Because what I hear is that there's the 29th of May, then five to ten days, and then the 27th of June. What happened to the 20 or so days in between that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Nothing much. We stayed in the house. We could hear the sounds of cars passing by, all sorts of vulgar songs being sung. Every night soldiers would pass, but we stayed locked up in that house, expecting someone to eventually turn up and open the door. But we didn't know where to go until that night, the 27th of June, when Milan Lukic emerged at our door, too, and knocked on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could you explain again how to get towards Bikavac from Dusce?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: From Dusce. All right. Where were we in the house? So this was towards the top of Dusce. So we headed for the woods. We headed up for the woods, behind trees, that sort of thing, plum trees, all sorts of things; and then we continued walking up, and as soon as we reached the road, the road to Bikavac, from Dusce to Bikavac connecting the two, we took the road that was there. It's a road like any other. So we climbed all the way to the top, and then in order to reach Baksa's house, we had to descend, go down a relatively mild slope before we arrived at her house. We didn't have long to go, but we spent that night in someone's yard, or rather -- but early the next morning, we reached Baksa's house, and we took the main road to get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And Baksa's house, what was -- what neighbourhood was that in? Did it have a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I don't really know. I didn't ask. But it was the first row of houses from Dusce. When you take the road from Dusce, those were the first houses you came across on the left-hand side. If you were headed out of town or from Bikavac, they would have been on your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: During the 20 days in between your arrival there and the 27th, how did you get food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: There were other empty houses there with food in them, houses that had been abandoned in a hurry. Later on, there was looting and all sorts of things going on, but we walked by night. We would go to these houses. If the doors were locked, we never broke in; but if houses were opened, we would go and have a look. You need something to eat, and you don't care about anything else. You're scared sick and hungry, but you're not really that hungry on account of all the fear, so it's not like we needed that much food because all we could think about was our fear. It's not like we were thinking about eating. We were too scared to even think about eating all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, it's on the 27th of June that you say you saw a Passat drive into the garden of the house "in which we were staying." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it drive by. I didn't see them until they entered the house. I could see the light on in the hallway and the car's brake lights outside our house; and then Milan Lukic, accompanied by this group of armed soldiers, entered the house. This was nighttime. We couldn't see the car approaching, and we hadn't realised that they were there until they knocked on our door.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm talking about 8.00 in the evening, before it got dark.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Well, it was already dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it's this time that you also identify Mitar Vasiljevic as being there, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes, but Mrs. Baksa and my mother-in-law recognised the man. I did not personally recognise him. I didn't personally identify him. I heard this from the lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you ever go to the restaurant in Panos where Mitar worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Did I go there? I was a child. Later when I got married, well, I didn't have time to go out with my husband because there were rumours in Visegrad at the time already. People didn't really go out much. Certain rumours had started spreading, and when I went to the secondary school I didn't go to cafes and to hotels. I was young at the time. Perhaps I would occasionally go to a cafe in Visegrad, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Please describe what Mitar Vasiljevic was wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: He was in black. He was wearing a black hat. He was quite corpulent. He had a belly. That's what he looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What was his hair colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I couldn't see because he was wearing a big black hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Anything distinguishable about his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: He had a very red face which I recognised because he had this very red face, this bloated face.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At this time, though, you indicate that they all -- these soldiers all immediately started threatening you, threatening to slit your throats, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: If they found women from the area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And they did this mistreatment for half an hour, you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Roughly speaking. I don't know for how long exactly. It was between 20 minutes and half an hour. It never occurred to me to look at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you say that the windows were drawn shut but the door was open, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: The door remained open, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And anyone could have looked out at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes. You could see from the corridor, you could see the parked car -- the car parked in front of the house. You could see its headlights on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was it running?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: The music was so loud that it was impossible to hear whether it was running or not, but the music was so loud and the songs were of such a kind that I didn't even ask myself whether the car was running or not. The songs were very vulgar and very loud.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What direction does this doorway face, north, south, east or west?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking in front of me now, so -- yes, it was like that, straight ahead, towards the east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, we're going to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the absence of Judge Van Den Wyngaert, Judge David and I sit pursuant to the provisions of Rule 15 bis. There is a whistling sound ... Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. VG-119, what I'm going to ask the court assistant to do right now is show you a photograph that has already been admitted as P33 for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can the witness be handed that photograph, please, and I'd like the witness to be able to mark up this photograph. Could it be removed from the plastic sleeve, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, can you see the photograph clearly, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph as an aerial view of the Bikavac neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would like you to locate the home that you stayed in Bikavac for the 20 or so days.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: It goes up from Dusce, from Dusce --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, we cannot -- we --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Baksa's house is down below, and the house I was in was the house in Visoce house, the Visoce house up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you see Baksa's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I can't see the exact house, but it's here. The house is here at the beginning of this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, then, I'd like you to circle the house where you believe Baksa's house to be and put a "B" in it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: This is where it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could you please circle the home that is Veljan's home, and put a "V" in the circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have not seen any marks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say where it was exactly. I know it was the Visoce house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Is there a technology problem? I'm unable to see the marks that the witness has made.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And just looking at the marks, ma'am, the first circle that indicates Baksa's house looks like it's five houses in there. Can you tell exactly which one it is, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, sir, I can't. I can't say which house it is exactly. I know it was at the beginning and that the house is here in the first row of houses to the left. I know there were three houses. I can't remember how many there were in front, but I think that it was these three houses here because the house below didn't have a facade - I can remember that - Osman's house below. Baksa's, which was also Safet's house, didn't have a facade, whereas these other houses had a facade. Baksa's house had a facade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'd like you to circle, please, which house was Veljan's house where you stayed until the 27th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I couldn't say exactly. It was above Visoce, so that would be this group of houses here, but I don't know which one exactly. I couldn't say for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Will you please put a "V" in that "C" or semicircle that you drew.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could you please find Meho Aljic's house, please, and circle that one and put an "M" in it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I can't say where it is for sure. I wouldn't like to make a mistake. In this circle here, where I stayed -- well, I don't know which house it is exactly because I didn't know his house from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you put an arrow at some corner of the photograph pointing north.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could you put a small "N" at the end of that arrow to indicate that that's the direction of north, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would submit to you, looking at the photograph, ma'am -- well, rather, in your statement of 1994, you indicate that the home of Veljan was 1 kilometre away from the earlier house, and that doesn't appear to be 1 kilometre.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Well, I can't be precise. I didn't measure distances. I didn't have time for that, sir. I went there to find shelter, but as for how far away it was, I didn't measure it, and I don't know why you're asking me about this. Is it that important? Is it that important to know whether it's a kilometre away or 20 steps away? What's important is that I was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, the Prosecutor used an hour and 34 minutes. You have used just about one hour, and at a maximum you will have another 34 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, on direct examination earlier and on cross-examination, you indicated that you had to go through the woods and up and down a hill when you were travelling between the two homes; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if he's going to refer to prior testimony, I would request that we see the exact place where he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, she just agreed with me. Do we -- I mean, I don't have the cite to the transcript. I'm going off my own memory. I don't have assistants that move and do that in the short time of the break. I'm just going off my notes and my memory. I didn't make a page reference in my notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, in the circumstances, yes, since the witness has agreed. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And on the photograph, I don't see where there would be a trip through the forest from the area that is marked with a "B" to the area that is marked with a "V"; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Sir, it wasn't a forest such as you would imagine. I said there were some plum trees, some fir trees. It started here. You can't see this area here. So this is where you start entering Bikavac. It's when you enter from Dusce and head towards Bikavac. I didn't say it was a dense forest. There were some plum trees, small trees there. It was a modest affair. It wasn't a huge forest that would look like a real forest. We're talking about urban settlements, not about villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, could you show us the route that you left when you decided to escape from the house marked with a "V"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: We headed off in the direction of this -- of these houses. We passed through the settlement towards Seganje, to the Seganje settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Please use the marker to draw the line that you travelled. Please put the photograph down on the table so that you can -- it's a little more stable, and you could use --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the court assistant give her a different colour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is the route we took to pass through the settlement. We passed through the settlement and went up to Seganje, towards the forest or the woods up here. When we arrived up here, we went as far as we could. We passed by all the houses, and then we passed through the woods, and then above this settlement there's a forest. We passed through the forest to Okrugla. We no longer went through the settlement but through the forest to the village of Okrugla.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could you please sign and date that photograph, ma'am, at the bottom in the white.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: The date today, the 1st of September -- October.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And for clarification, ma'am, isn't it true that you are not able to circle the home that you believed to be Meho Aljic? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I want to be precise, so I can't circle that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you walked by the home, how many metres were you from the home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Very close, perhaps 2 or 3 metres away from it. There was a path that passed by that house, the path that we took.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And was it on your right or your left as you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: It was on my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was it in rubble as if it had burned to the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: The house's roof had burnt. There was no roof, and you could still smell the smoke coming out of the house. It had already burnt down; the roof had already burnt down, but we didn't linger there. We moved on as soon as it was possible for us to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long after Milan Lukic supposedly came the second time and you fainted or pretended to faint did you leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Well, not even a month later. His -- the second time he appeared, it was at night, and then after that it wasn't even after a month had expired.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm talking about the evening of the 27th of June. You indicated that Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic returned; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you pretended to faint; and therefore, you escaped being taken away, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes, and not just myself but all the others for whom Milan Lukic said that they should go with him. So I saved the girls who were supposed to be taken away that night too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And during that night, you didn't see a lot of activity. I mean, if you're going to move 70 people in and out of a neighbourhood or collect people from a neighbourhood, that should have been quite a commotion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Sir, there was loud music that you could hear in front of our door, and the people -- the inhabitants weren't scattered around; they were always in groups. So it was enough to have a few houses close to each other to gather that number of individuals. If they'd only focused on us and another few houses, they would have gathered 70 individuals very rapidly. They wouldn't have needed much time to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you spent 20 days approximately in this house. Didn't you socialise with the people that had retreated to the Bikavac neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, sir. We couldn't move around. If you found a house to stay in, you would stay there. All you did was wait for someone to come and knock on your door, so we didn't think about socialising at all. We remained in the houses we were in. We never left the house. We never went anywhere. Only Ms. Baksa sometimes took some food to her children behind the house; it was to that bricked-in location, but we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The night of the 27th, you didn't see a glow in the sky that was a fire so close to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Well, I didn't look outside the house because the shutters were closed; the door's closed. We were sitting to the right in the corner. We wouldn't look at the door. We were in the corner to the right, so I wasn't sitting by the door and looking out to see whether anything was burning or whether anyone was out there. We just remained sitting there quietly and thought that the gentlemen were perhaps still outside the door. It never occurred to me that there might be a fire or that I should go and have a look to see what was happening. I didn't have the time; I didn't have the courage to go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You mean to tell me you didn't hear gun-fire, even if the radio was playing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: The music was so loud, believe me, that it was impossible for us to listen to it. The music was so loud. The songs were of such a kind that I didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you didn't hear grenades going off, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you indicated earlier that the house of Meho Aljic was only one house away; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That's not what the witness stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I believe you were going to answer, ma'am. Can you answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No. Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just let's -- you must state the evidence correctly. What did the witness state, Ms. Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure she was asked this exact question, and that's why I object and would ask the Defence counsel to refer again to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Actually, I'm referring to her statement of January 1994 where she states that they continued towards Meho Aljic's house, "which was next door but one."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not a satisfactory way to proceed, Mr. Alarid, and you must know that. Your question was: "But you indicated earlier." Earlier when?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I should have stayed within the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In her direct examination or in a previous statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll be more specific, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you recall in your earlier statement of January 1994 indicating that Meho Aljic's was next door but one to the house where you were staying?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I have the statement in front of me, and I don't see that. I would like Defence counsel --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Page 5 in the English version, middle of the page. "Aljic" is in all capitals underneath "Vasiljevic."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, counsel is saying that in your earlier statement of January 1994, you said that Meho Aljic's house was next door but one to the house where you were staying. Do you have anything to say about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that. The house was perhaps the third or fourth house from the house I was staying in, but the distance between the houses -- well, I don't know what the distance was exactly, but the house was perhaps the second or the third house away. But it wasn't as if they were just short distances between the houses, as a result of which I should have been able to hear shooting or other things. I can't confirm what he has said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that earlier in your testimony you stated that the house of Meho Aljic was right behind the house where you were staying, would that refresh your recollection, referring to page 26, line 14 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Sir, all I'm telling you about is what I personally know. When Zehra came to the door, she said, "Do you know what happened in the house nearby? 70 people were burnt." So I can't be more precise about these things that happened at night. I passed by a house after 2.00 in the morning. All I know is that the house was not very far away, but it wasn't that close either; so it wasn't possible to hear what you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: -- I believe -- the lines that Defence counsel quotes does not say exactly what he said. It's referring to a road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just read it for me, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It says: "They spoke to us at the door. We asked her inside, but she refused. She said she had fled. There was another house further down the road right behind our house." "Further down the road right behind our house" is what she said. She didn't say it was "right behind."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it on the basis of that statement, Mr. Alarid, that you have put your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That was an addendum. The original course was out of the actual original statement of 1994 where she stated that it was next door but one, and -- but today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In any event, now you must move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you indicate that this evening was the first time you met Zehra Turjacanin, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you had been in this neighbourhood over 20 days, and you had never come across her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Well, I said that we didn't move around. I never left the house. My mother-in-law would only go from Baksa's house to the village. I didn't move around. I didn't meet anyone. I only socialised with my family and with Baksa's family. As I said, I never left the house. I don't know who was in Bikavac and who was moving around.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you find it illogical that if the residents or people were being rounded up to be burned alive in a house that your home and all the occupants that you were staying with were spared?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Well, sir, ask your accused. I'm not accused; he is. He knows why he didn't burn us. I can't tell you why we weren't affected. Perhaps it was God's will. I don't know. I'm not the person on trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, but in your earlier testimony, page 27, line 22, you indicated that the smoke rising of the house -- excuse me. "When we left the house and reached another house, the one behind us, we realised there was smoke rising out of that house." That was your testimony from earlier. So it seems to indicate that this house was extremely near your house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No. I said when we set off, we passed by a house and there was smoke coming out of it. I didn't say it was the second, third, fourth, et cetera. It was not far away. It wasn't very far away, but it wasn't very close either. So that's the house that we came across. There was this house some distance away, and there was smoke still coming out of it. It was further above. And we took a path, and a metre or two away from the path, you could see that there was still smoke coming out of the house. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you met Ms. Turjacanin, you indicate that her lips were burned so much so that she could not drink or smoke a cigarette?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe that that's what she testified to when she first saw this witness at the door. That was later on, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We can break that up into two questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it true that when you first saw her that her lips were burnt and her -- describe, also, any other burns on her upper torso that you witnessed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Sir, I saw that this part of the woman, as low as her breasts and her hands and her arms had been burnt. You could see the flesh here. Her hair had been singed. When I saw her at the door, I couldn't see what her lips looked like, what her teeth looked like. She had been burned. I saw her singed hair, and I saw her arms and the flesh dangling from her arms. I think that should be enough. I think what I have said about this event is sufficient. I don't like remembering the woman at the time. She looked so terrible. But when I helped her that night, well, the burns on her lips were hard, and you could see the terrible state her hands were in. It's difficult to experience such a thing, so I don't know how you can ask me about such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, you -- I noticed, and letting the record reflect, that when you said of "the flesh was showing," where you pointed to your chest, and you also said that her breasts were burnt. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I said the arms, the forearms. This is where the flesh was hanging off the bones. She had burns here on her hair, burned dry, and she was wearing some sort of a dress. That was also in tatters and hanging off her body, but that's all I could see as far as her body was concerned. The only part that was entirely uncovered was the face, a part of the breast, and the forearms. She was probably wearing short sleeves. So when I say "flesh hanging off the bone," I mean the forearms. I didn't mean the breast. I don't think I ever said that. The burns here, that's what I was indicating.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you're indicating that there was burns in -- like an exposed area of a V of a dress, sort of similar to what you're wearing? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: The neck, yes, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were there burns below the neckline?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Like this, as I said, the whole thing. That's as far as I could tell when this woman was standing at the door. She held her arms like this, and she was all trembling. The flesh was dangling from the bone. If you get just a very small burn, you know how much that can hurt, and this woman was burned all over. She was so sick that she had to go and lie down. They were carrying her already, and when she lay down, she hurt too much. She was sick with pain. It's not that she didn't want to go. She would have come with us, but she was in such a bad shape, and she had been so burned up that she simply couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you say -- remind me, please. You say that they were carrying her. Who was carrying her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Her brother, he was, and some other soldiers who were with him. I don't know who it was, but I know that her brother carried her, Zehra said, and when the soldiers came, she said that they had had to carry her. She wasn't able to walk on her own, that the -- that branches while walking through the woods would brush her in passing, and that hurt like hell. I heard her screams and her moans as we were walking through the woods. She'd be brushed by a branch in passing, and she would scream out. She wanted us to scratch and pat her head to make it better. She was on the verge of a breakdown. That's how much suffering she was going through. It was hell. There.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But I thought she didn't travel with you away from the Bikavac neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: She didn't. We went there and we said what had happened once we'd crossed over to the Muslim-held territory. But when we said that, her brother that night went over and brought his sister back, along with the other soldiers. That's what I'm telling you. I'm not telling you that she had been with us because she wasn't. She wasn't able to walk. We couldn't carry her, and we didn't know at the time that the men would eventually come with us, the couple of men who did eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long a walk was it from Bikavac to the Muslim-held territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: We walked the whole night. We would stop at houses, houses that were burned down, and then we would look to see whether there were some Serbs still remaining in the area, and then behind those houses we realised that there were Serbs houses, for example, and someone lived there, and then we would go further up so that the whole night we walked on and on, and we crawled, and we crawled our way to Okrugla. So it wasn't before next morning that we arrived at Okrugla. That night, this whole time, we spent on the move until the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you did -- were able to spend a considerable amount of time with Ms. Turjacanin, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes, in Okrugla I did. And then while going through the woods, sometimes she would ask me, and I'd scratch her head where it hurt. In Medjedja, she was staying in this medical station where they were treating her. They shaved her head. They dressed the burns on her arms. And I was some way down the road from there in a different house, and I would sometimes go and see her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: For how many days did you spend with her attending to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: What do you mean, in Medjedja, or the whole thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The whole thing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: The whole thing? Five days on the road, I saw her every day. The day in Okrugla adds up to six days and then every single day until Zehra was moved from there, which means another ten days that I spent seeing her in Medjedja, which would add up to a total of nearly 20 days, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how many times did you hear her tell her story?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Back in Okrugla, when the soldiers asked, I heard from the soldiers. They were telling me what Zehra had told them, the account she had given them. It was difficult for her to speak, and I only heard her talk about this the one time she was interviewed by those journalists, which I believe I've mentioned already. I told you about the interview, when she was interviewed by journalists, and that was the first time I caught on to the fact that Sredoje Lukic had been involved as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your ICTY statement of the 13th of January, 2000, you indicate in there that you have given two statements two times before to the Tribunal, "last time during the winter last year." Do you recall when in 1999 you gave a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the reason I ask you that is we did not receive a copy of any statements from 1999 for you from the ICTY, and so I'm trying to get more of an approximation. Can you give me the month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically. I provided four statements. I know that I provided four statements, and I stand by them. My position remains unchanged. But I can't be more specific than that about what you're asking me about simply because I didn't take any notes. I didn't write anything down. I was interviewed. I gave those statements. I know who I gave them to and when in the sense of giving a statement to such and such a person at Gorazde, for example, and then making a statement to the Hague Tribunal and Women Victims of War and -- this is stuff that I said before, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When did you become a member of the Women Victims of War?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the form of the question. She never said she was a member of the Women Victims of War.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's suggestio falsi, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never got anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's suggestio falsi. She never said she was a member of the Women Victims of War.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll just ask the question directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you a member of the Women Victims of War?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How many times have you met with their representatives, anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Just the one time I gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Have you ever met with Bakira, the president of the association?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Only when I provided the statement to her. I did say that, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So she -- excuse me. So she was present for that statement specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you ever have phone conversations at any time with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No. I was never in touch again with anyone I was providing my statements to except for those specific occasions when I gave my statements, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you -- were you able to watch the television programmes of Turjacanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No. The place where I live, we don't have this network, not the sort of network that would allow me to follow the trial, not at my place. This is a federal programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you -- did you actually, though, watch her being videotaped by the journalists as she told her story?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: A moment to confer, Your Honour. I think I'm done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions. At this time, I would like to introduce the marked photograph as well as the 17 January 1994 statement, uploaded as 1D10-2812.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we'll admit that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would also introduce 1D10-2856, which is the statement that was disavowed by the witness; and I would introduce 1D10-2830, which is the 13 January 2000 ICTY statement; and I would introduce 1D10-2844, which is the 19 April 2008 ICTY statement, and all under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: My preference is for submissions for the admission of exhibits to be made individually during the testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: All right. I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now we have about, what, five or six pieces of evidence to admit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the photograph will become Exhibit 156 under seal. The first statement will become 1D57, under seal. The second statement will become Exhibit 1D58, under seal. The third statement will become Exhibit 1D59, under seal. And the fourth statement will become Exhibit 1D60, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening, madam.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My name is Djuro Cepic, and I represent Sredoje Lukic. Before I ask you a question, I want to say on behalf of my team how sorry I am that you lost your nearest and dearest during the war. I want to express my regret for all the suffering that you had to go through.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I would ask you to please listen closely to my questions and if possible, provide clear and brief answers to help us get through this as quickly as possible. Do you understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam, I would like to put to you that your memory is not reliable. Some of the things you state are not as presented before. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes, I understand you, but what's all this about presenting? What do you think is not accurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We're getting to that at a later stage. First, I would like to refer to the photograph where you made certain markings for Mr. Alarid. I think this is 1D56.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could that exhibit please be placed in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, my learned friend, asked you about Meho Aljic's house, but you couldn't say specifically where it was, pinpoint the location. And then at page 62, line 5, you said that it was inside this circle. The circle you had in mind was probably the circle containing Mr. Veljan's house and marked as a "V," right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: That was the house where I was staying when this occurred. It was inside that circle. I didn't say where. I said it was inside that circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You did specify. You said "inside this circle," inside this circle right here. You marked two circles, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I marked the circle where I was staying in Baksa Ramovic's place. That was before the burning, and then I went over to a different house, and that was the other house that I marked with a "V." That's further north. The gentleman told me to mark that, right? And then I said inside this circle somewhere -- yes, yes. Yes, the other circle that I drew, the other place that I was staying at, not Baksa's house but the other house. That's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this clarification. I was a little uncertain about this, and I thank you for this clarification. So the circle marked with the letter "V," right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I don't have the drawing in front of me. That's why I'm asking. Thank you very much. Thank you. Thank you for this clarification. Madam, today at page 34 of the transcript, you mentioned that Zehra's interview was the first time you heard that in addition to Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic, Sredoje Lukic was around during this incident, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You go on to describe him as having fairer hair than Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes. His hair was fairer than Milan Lukic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And shorter, too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Last week in this courtroom, on the 24th of September, to be more specific, in this courtroom, there was a gentleman who said the same thing as you, or rather, testified about the same circumstances, and he said that Milan Lukic was taller than Sredoje. He went on to say that Milan Lukic was taller than Sredoje by about 20 centimetres. Would you agree with his assessment?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection to the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I really couldn't say. I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The difference in height, your take on it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I really can't say. I wasn't able to judge that. My perception was not particularly specific that night. I was in no position to pay attention to that sort of thing. The one thing I did realise was that Milan Lukic was the tallest of all of them, but this wasn't what I was thinking about at the time. My mind wasn't set on this. All I cared about was escaping alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I fully understand what you're saying, but we do need to clarify a detail or two. Please show some understanding. Please try to think back and remember in the roughest of terms what the difference in height would be, 20, 15, 5 centimetres, whatever.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, sir. I'm sorry. I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So you're not able to help us, are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, unfortunately I can't say that. That's what I'm telling you. I don't want to go wrong on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that he was shorter than Milan Lukic, but by about how much exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The witness has answered. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When you say fairer hair, that means blonde, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, not blonde. Fairer than Milan's hair. Milan's hair was black. His was a hue fairer but not blonde. Blonde is a different thing altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about his sporting a moustache?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about a beard? Do you remember that by any chance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Same height as Mitar Vasiljevic, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I can't say that either. Mitar Vasiljevic was wearing a huge hat, a very tall one, which made his head look taller. It was a large-sized hat, which probably made him appear taller. It was huge and black, the hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the other persons who were there? What were they wearing in terms of head-gear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: They were rather on the young side. They must have been my age or thereabouts, quite young. I don't know what they were doing all of this for. I was wondering at the time. I mean, after all, these people were my generation. We were the same age.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic was perhaps one or two or perhaps three years older than you, right? He was Milan's age or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I really don't know, sir. All I know is my husband's age, what it was at the time, and Milan Lukic was the same generation, the same age.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In the roughest of terms, Sredoje was your husband's age? Younger? Slightly older, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: I never said he was younger. Who said that? He wasn't younger than either Milan Lukic or my husband. I never said younger. I said there were other men there who were quite young, the other soldiers who were there in the same group. The people who were with them were practically youngsters. They were just young lads, my age. I don't know what on earth they were doing with these people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Previously, you told us that they were wearing Serbian sajkaca caps or hats, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes. When they took my husband away, those lads who were with Milan Lukic were wearing those caps. That's what I said. I don't know about the burning of that house and the people in it. I just told you about Mitar Vasiljevic and his hat. That's all I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about the rest of them? They weren't wearing any sort of head-gear at all, right? Bare-headed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: That's right, yes. Not the three of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps give us a hand with this any way you can. We're trying to identify this person that you believed to be there and to be involved in this incident. Anything at all you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Which person do you mean? In relation to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what I'm saying. The one who was shorter than Milan Lukic. Was there any distinguishing feature, something that would set him apart from the others there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No. They were all wearing sort of the same clothes, but Milan Lukic was wearing camouflage and the rest, civilian clothes. There was no particular detail, no distinguishing feature that I might be able to remember. It's a bit silly to be nitpicking like this. I'm trying to piece this together, but I simply can't for the life of me remember any small, distinguishing feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Civilian clothes, you said. Jeans, perhaps? Another kind of trousers? Jeans died in black?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: The only thing I remember is that Mitar Vasiljevic was wearing black, plus this hat that I mentioned before. But as for this other man, believe me, I don't remember what he was wearing. It was Mitar Vasiljevic of all of them who looked the bulkiest, the biggest somehow, and then this huge black hat, Milan Lukic, it was someone I knew personally because I'd seen him before.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I understand that. Yes, right. Mitar Vasiljevic who was massive, so he cut a dominant figure in relation to the young lads there, and the other person you believed was Sredoje Lukic because he was so big and massive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes. He was quite a big man, red-faced, with a huge head and that large hat that he was wearing. He was elegantly plump, to put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And he was broader and taller than the other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: No, no, no. I didn't mean it that way. It was just that hat that he was wearing. I never said that he was taller than the others. I never said that. You're asking me if he was taller or not. All I'm trying to tell you is the way he struck me with that hat and his body being a bit more corpulent than that of the others. But I didn't say that he was necessarily taller than anyone else in that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mitar was the fattest, if you like, the biggest in that group.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-119
utterances.text: Yes, the biggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, madam.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I would like to start a new topic, so if we start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take the adjournment now and start again tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of October, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.07 p.m.,
